correctness.rationale: For each proper ideal I inside radical m=⊕x_i k[x_i]/(x_i^{n_i}), the exact intersections I∩U_i determine unique b_i. Multiplication by x_i shows I lies between K_b and K_b^+, and its quotient is an axis-avoiding subspace L≤k^{S(b)}; conversely each such L is stable under every x_i and has the prescribed intersections. Gaussian-binomial inclusion-exclusion yields h_{s,d}(q), and grouping b_i gives Z_A(T). Pairing x_i^a with x_i^{n_i−a} is nondegenerate and A-balanced on m; orthogonal complementation of ideals is an involution reversing dimension N−d, proving proper-ideal palindromicity for every field. Independently exhaustive GF2 subspace computations matched the formula for length tuples (2,2),(3,2),(3,3),(3,3,2),(2,2,2,2).
